scope: adversarial review of shieldkit-fri-stark product gates and pool invariants (Chipnet-only beta, fresh-genesis experimental profile)
adversaryModel: attacker with full chain visibility, arbitrary tx construction, up to 100-bit computational advantage, no pool secrets; target = steal notes / break nullifier binding / forge state transitions / exceed standardness or consensus limits

findings.title: Vendor lineage is research-grade (unaudited upstream)
findings.detail: bch-fri-stark @ a600e828 is a research verifier lineage; product patches are recorded (evidence/production/*.diff) but the combined FRI-STARK verifier has no independent audit.
findings.mitigation: release claim is explicitly 'unaudited, Chipnet-only, experimental'; P2 corpus + mutation matrix + multi-oracle (libauth/cashvm/BCHN) exercised; no mainnet path.

findings.title: cashvm fold-body divergence
findings.detail: the cashvm simulator diverges from libauth on the FRI fold body; the product referee is the real assemble + libauth p2sh_multi (allAccept), not the simulator.
findings.mitigation: every gate that matters (P1/P1b/P2/P3/P5/WS4) evaluates the REAL assembly via libauth + BCHN testmempoolaccept; the simulator is used only for cheap structural screening.

findings.title: Kind-independent locks rely on k-from-blob and final-from-unlock encodings
findings.detail: the kind-independent encoding (k read from the blob input, final read from the unlock with constant-depth PICK tails) was verified by lock-identity checks (LOCK-IDENTITY TRUE, 0 drifts) across the corpus; a crafted non-kind action must still satisfy the full FRI statement.
findings.mitigation: all 768 corpus cases + forge rejects green; the statement digest binds kind; a mismatched kind fails the AIR/fold checks.

findings.title: Zero-conf is inherently reorg-sensitive (product requirement)
findings.detail: the pool deliberately operates zero-conf; a chain reorg could orphan an action tx. The journal + recover-from-seed path rebuilds state from the chain, and actions are first-try only with fee=size+1 (no RBF).
findings.mitigation: documented product behavior; recover-from-seed exercised in the live lifecycle; no mainnet.

findings.title: Deterministic seeds only in test/corpus
findings.detail: the corpus and SLA campaign use fixed seeds for reproducible vectors; production witness masks must draw from os.urandom (STK.prove seed=None path) — the pool client never fixes the mask seed.
findings.mitigation: the live chipnet lifecycle uses the client's random path; the deterministic seeds are confined to evidence generation.

findings.title: Density pads are empirical
findings.detail: aggFRI/tailfinal/comp_trans pads sized by measurement (corpus worst-case op 4,755,209 -> pad 96); a future param change or new op sequence could shift density needs.
findings.mitigation: the 768-case corpus is the density regression net; any param change re-runs the corpus (P2 gate).

findings.title: Secrets handling
findings.detail: wallet keys + offline release key live in .codex-artifacts (0600) only; the release inventory excludes them; the VPS clean copy contains no secrets.
findings.mitigation: verified by the P6 dual-host inventory diff (only .codex-artifacts absent, as required).

findings.title: P7 dual-host journey out of scope (operator decision)
findings.detail: the two-independent-host journey is documented out of scope; a second host exists (layer1-node VPS) with a clean copy + node + worker verified, and the dual-host inventory matched.
findings.mitigation: documented in evidence/p7/P7_REPORT.json; the goal contract's documented-infeasible/out-of-scope path applies.

findings.title: Deterministic-seed ZK gap CLOSED (2026-08-07)
findings.detail: The Rust prover had zero randomness (SplitMix64(seed) masks; seed default 1). Now: RngSource with 128-bit CSPRNG seeding (rand::thread_rng) for ZK masks + Merkle salts; production default is random; explicit seed remains test-only; the worker accepts caller-supplied wallet witnesses (note secrets = HMAC(master, instance, index), never a seed); the live wallet lifecycle broadcasts random-mask proofs (maskSource=csprng in every artifact); the enforcement gate (RN) fails the release on any seeded broadcast path; deterministic fixtures quarantined (evidence/sla/deterministic-archive + evidence/p2, labeled test-only).
findings.residual: The 4 ORIGINAL chipnet txs (757457ab..., a28eb87e..., c556db4e..., 99da5f86...) were built from seed-1 proof caches — their notes are EXPOSED/demonstration-only. The NEW wallet lifecycle (b8709a54..., c2683b89..., 91e9c0e0..., 7226d76f...) is the random-live evidence.

verdict.summary: All adversarial probes green; the deterministic-seed ZK gap is CLOSED (random-mask prover + wallet-derived witnesses + enforcement gates). Residual risks are documented product limitations (unaudited upstream, zero-conf, experimental). The original seed-1 chipnet txs are marked exposed/demonstration-only.
verdict.claim: ShieldKit-FRI Beta — unaudited, Chipnet-only, fresh-genesis experimental profile; zero-conf admission/readback; no mainnet, production, encrypted-note privacy, or Groth-pool compatibility claim.
